title: Condorcet Winners and the Not-All-Equal Condition
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f$ map the $n$-dimensional sign cube to $\\{ -1,1 \\}$, and let $p$ assign one of the six strict rankings of three candidates to each of $n$ voters. For each of the three pairwise contests, let the societal outcome be the sign returned by $f$ on the voters’ pairwise preferences. The indicator that this outcome has a Condorcet winner equals $1$ precisely when its three signs are not all equal, and equals $0$ otherwise.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ maps the $n$-dimensional sign cube to a sign
$p$ assigns a ranking of three candidates to each of $n$ voters
